rmb_to_hkd_note: Approximate mid-market rate as of June 2026. Used to convert RMB intrinsic value per share to HKD for comparison against the HKEX-listed price. All DCF inputs and outputs are in RMB millions unless labelled HKD.

inputs.shares_note: Post-split. BYD implemented an 8-for-10 bonus share distribution and 12-for-10 capital reserve capitalisation in July 2025, increasing total shares from ~3.04bn to ~9.12bn (a ~3.0x factor). Use 9,117.2M for all per-share calculations.
inputs.cash_note: FY2025 year-end (Dec 2025). Cash & equivalents from balance sheet. Down from 102,257M at FY2024 due to capex cycle peak.
inputs.total_debt_note: FY2025 year-end total borrowings (includes both short-term 41,128M and long-term 69,372M per Q3 2025 disclosures). Surged from 41,652M at FY2024 year-end as overseas factory construction was funded via debt. Q1 2026 total debt rose further to ~135,816M.
inputs.net_debt_note: Positive = net debt position. FY2025: total_debt 110,500M minus cash 68,395M = net debt 42,105M. BYD moved from net cash ~60,605M (FY2024) to net debt as capex cycle peaked and balance sheet leverage increased materially.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 FCF = operating CF 59,136M minus capex 156,808M = -97,672M. Negative FCF reflects capex cycle peak (overseas factory buildout: Hungary, Thailand, Brazil expansion, domestic charging infrastructure). FCF projections use revenue-based normalised FCF margins rather than this distorted base.

historical_growth.revenue_5yr_cagr_note: FY2020 to FY2025: 153,469M -> 803,965M. Reflects extraordinary NEV market penetration surge; not forward-replicable at current scale.
historical_growth.eps_3yr_cagr_note: FY2022 to FY2025, split-adjusted (3.133x factor applied to pre-split EPS). FY2022 EPS 5.71 adj -> 1.82; FY2025 EPS 3.58. Decline reflects margin compression despite revenue growth.
historical_growth.eps_5yr_cagr_note: FY2020 to FY2025, split-adjusted. FY2020 EPS 1.47 adj -> 0.47; FY2025 EPS 3.58. 5yr figure distorted by FY2020 pandemic-year trough.
historical_growth.equity_3yr_cagr_note: FY2022 to FY2025: 111,029M -> 246,275M. Boosted by USD5.6bn H-share placing in March 2025 and perpetual bond issuance; organic equity growth is lower.
historical_growth.equity_5yr_cagr_note: FY2020 to FY2025: 56,874M -> 246,275M. Capital raise inflates; normalize for forward projections.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FCF CAGRs not calculable as FY2025 FCF is negative (-97,672M) due to capex cycle peak. FCF projections use forward-normalised FCF margin on revenue. Historical reference: FY2024 FCF margin was 4.6% (36,094M / 777,103M).
historical_growth.growth_rate_note: Historical revenue CAGRs (23.8% / 39.3%) are backward-looking and not forward-replicable at RMB 804bn revenue scale. FY2025 revenue grew only 3.5% YoY; Q1 2026 was -11.8% YoY. Forward base rate anchored on analyst consensus for FY2026: ~RMB 850-900bn revenue (+10-12%). Equity CAGR (30.4% / 34.1%) used as secondary check — inflated by the USD5.6bn March 2025 capital raise. Growth decelerates across Y1-Y5.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (50.2%) diverges 15.8pp from Equity 5yr CAGR (34.1%) — within the 30pp threshold. Revenue 5yr CAGR (39.3%) diverges 5.2pp from Equity 5yr CAGR — within tolerance. No automatic flag triggered. However, all historical CAGRs are materially above sustainable forward rates given the FY2025 revenue growth of only 3.5% and negative Q1 2026.

base.growth_rationale: Aligned with FY2026 analyst consensus (~RMB 850-900bn, +10-12% YoY). Decelerates from Y3 as domestic market matures and the base grows. Overseas export growth (guided 43% YoY to 1.5M units) partially offsets domestic declines. Y5 rate of 7% reflects a stabilising but still-growing international business.
base.fcf_margin_rationale: Modest FCF margin recovery to 5.5% from FY2025 trough (-12.2% actual FCF margin, distorted by extraordinary capex of 156bn). FCF should normalise from H2 2026 as overseas factory construction completes. FY2024 normalised FCF margin was 4.6%. 5.5% assumes moderate capex tapering and operating margin stabilisation.
base.wacc_rationale: 11%: risk-free rate ~4.0% (China 10yr government bond), equity risk premium ~6.0%, China country risk premium ~1.0%. Beta effectively 1.0 (BYD is highly correlated with China macro sentiment and EV cycle). No size discount — BYD is a mega-cap.
base.terminal_growth_rationale: 3.0% — in line with Chinese nominal GDP long-run expectation (~4.5-5% nominal, discounted for BYD's non-China exposure maturity). BESS global growth sustains above-GDP trajectory at the group level.

bull.growth_rationale: Overseas exports hit 1.5M units FY2026 as guided (+43% YoY) and 2M+ units in FY2027. Hungary factory series production ramps through 2026 eliminating 17% EU additional tariff. BESS global #1 position grows 50%+ annually. Domestic premium brands (Denza, FANGCHENGBAO) drive ASP improvement. AI data center electronics gain traction. Bull scenario aligns with the overseas export inflection and technology leadership narrative.
bull.fcf_margin_rationale: Overseas revenue commands higher unit margins than domestic (per management). Capex cycle moderates from FY2025 peak as overseas factory buildout concludes. Electronics division pivot to AI infrastructure margin accretive. 7.5% would match FY2022 implied margins at peak scale leverage.
bull.wacc_rationale: 10%: overseas revenue diversification reduces China concentration risk. Hungary factory normalises EU tariff exposure. Successful capital allocation reduces leverage concerns.
bull.terminal_growth_rationale: 3.5%: BESS global leadership + ongoing overseas auto expansion sustains above-GDP trajectory. 119-country footprint diversifies geopolitical risk.

bear.growth_rationale: Q1 2026 -11.8% YoY persists through H1 2026; H2 recovery is modest and uneven. Domestic market share continues to erode from 21% toward 18% as Xiaomi YU7, Geely/Zeekr, Leapmotor, and Huawei-backed Aito attack simultaneously. EU tariff mitigation is delayed by Hungary factory ramp complexity and EU regulatory investigations. Price war compresses ASPs. Full-year FY2026 revenue barely above FY2025.
bear.fcf_margin_rationale: Continued capex for overseas factory ramp + 20,000 Flash Charging Station rollout + R&D exceeding 63bn/yr. FCF margin remains near FY2024 trough with no meaningful recovery. Operating cash flow weak given Q1 2026 -67% YoY decline.
bear.wacc_rationale: 12%: short-term borrowings +72% in Q1 2026; total debt at 110,500M+ and rising. FX losses materialising as RMB strengthens. Deteriorating domestic profitability raises risk premium.
bear.terminal_growth_rationale: 2.5%: below-GDP growth as commoditised EV market dynamics suppress long-term returns. Structural overcapacity in Chinese EV industry creates persistent margin headwind.

base.note: At HKD 72.65 current price, base case implies ~12.6% upside to HKD 81.80. Stock is modestly undervalued on base assumptions.

bull.note: Bull case requires overseas 1.5M+ units, FCF margin recovery to 7.5%, and WACC 10%. Achievable over 3-5 years but demands sustained execution across multiple geographies simultaneously.

bear.note: Bear case implies -55% downside. Requires domestic decline persisting, EU strategy stalling, and capex/leverage cycle not resolving.

base.note: To earn 15% CAGR to base terminal value (HKD 103.74), entry must be HKD 51.58 — 29% below current price.

bull.note: Bull terminal value is so high that even at HKD 72.65, you would achieve >15% CAGR — implying current price is comfortably below the 15% entry threshold in the bull case.

bear.note: Bear terminal value implies a 71% decline from current price would be required to achieve 15% CAGR — illustrating the severity of the bear scenario.

sensitivity.note: Base case growth rates [10,10,9,8,7%] and FCF margin 5.5% held constant. Values in HKD per share. Current price HKD 72.65 falls between WACC=11%/TG=2.5% (77.9) and WACC=12%/TG=3.5% (75.2).
sensitivity.current_price_marker: HKD 72.65 sits near WACC=11%/TG=2.0% (74.4) to WACC=12%/TG=3.0% (71.9) — current price is broadly fairly valued to slightly cheap, with upside if WACC re-rates toward 10-11% on improving execution

probability_weighted.note: Bull 25% / Base 50% / Bear 25%. Probability-weighted value of HKD 89.86 implies +23.7% upside from current HKD 72.65. The larger upside vs. the prior model (18.3%) reflects the price decline from HKD 75.95 to HKD 72.65 with intrinsic value unchanged.

reasonable_ranges.pe: 15-40x (growth-decelerating EV + battery + BESS maker; not pure-play auto at 8-12x, not pure-play growth at 50x+)

checks.comment: 21x is a reasonable multiple for a company with strong medium-term earnings recovery potential but near-term trough
10.6x is consistent with a high-quality auto/EV conglomerate at a moderately discounted valuation
0.85x is reasonable for a low-margin, high-volume business with improving international mix

41.9x on trough earnings is marginally above the normal range; however Q1 is acknowledged as likely profit trough (Goldman Sachs), making this a temporary distortion rather than a structural issue. No assumption auto-correction warranted.

sanity_check.overall_assessment: The base case valuation of HKD 81.80 per share implies multiples that are within reasonable bounds for BYD's current profile — a high-volume, vertically-integrated EV and battery maker transitioning from extraordinary domestic growth to a more measured international expansion phase. The 21x P/E on FY2025 earnings (which themselves are down 19% YoY) reflects a valid earnings recovery expectation. The current traded price of HKD 72.65 implies even cheaper multiples (P/E 18.6x, EV/EBITDA 9.5x, P/S 0.76x) — all within reasonable ranges. No assumption auto-correction was required.
sanity_check.ebitda_estimate_note: FY2025 EBITDA estimated as operating income (40,185M) + D&A estimate (~28,139M; ~3.5% of revenue). Official D&A not separately disclosed in available data.

valuation_philosophy.rationale: BYD's FY2025 FCF was -97,672M due to an extraordinary capex cycle (overseas factory construction across Hungary, Thailand, Brazil; domestic Flash Charging Station buildout; semiconductor and battery manufacturing expansion). Using raw FCF as a starting point would produce nonsensical negative valuations. Instead, projections use normalised FCF margins applied to projected revenues — consistent with the cyclical nature of BYD's capex programme. The 5.5% base FCF margin is below BYD's FY2022-2023 implied FCF margin (~10-11%) and modestly above FY2024 (4.6%), reflecting realistic capex moderation without assuming a return to peak levels.
key_risks_to_model: Domestic China NEV market share erosion accelerating beyond base assumptions (actual Q1 2026: -11.8% revenue, -55% profit YoY)
FX losses from RMB appreciation persisting or worsening as overseas mix exceeds 40%
Capex cycle extending beyond FY2026 due to additional factory commitments (Turkey, additional China charging)
EU regulatory risk to Hungary factory delaying European tariff relief
R&D spending (63bn+ pa, +17% YoY) growing faster than revenue, suppressing FCF recovery
valuation_philosophy.currency_note: All DCF inputs and cash flow projections are in RMB millions. Per-share intrinsic value is calculated in RMB (equity value / shares) then converted to HKD at 1 RMB = 1.09 HKD for apples-to-apples comparison against the HKEX-listed H-share price. The conversion rate of 1.09 is approximate for mid-2026 and should be updated if RMB/HKD moves materially.
valuation_philosophy.warning_banner: Q1 2026 RESULTS WERE A SIGNIFICANT MISS: Revenue -11.8% YoY, Net Profit -55% YoY. Goldman Sachs identifies this as the likely trough, but full recovery trajectory is uncertain. Treat Base Case as requiring monitored re-validation through Q2 2026 results.

key_observations: At HKD 72.65 (June 26, 2026), BYD trades at approximately 12.6% below the base case intrinsic value of HKD 81.80. This is modestly cheap on base assumptions with a slightly wider margin of safety than the prior model (8% at HKD 75.95).
The stock has declined from HKD 400+ mid-2025 post-split peak, representing a de-rating of ~82% — reflecting the FY2025 profit miss (-19% YoY) and Q1 2026 collapse (-55% YoY).

BYD moved from net cash (RMB 60,605M at FY2024) to net debt (RMB 42,105M at FY2025) in a single year — a structural change that reduces the net cash buffer supporting per-share value by approximately HKD 11.2 vs. the prior model.
The bull case (HKD 163.45, +125% upside) is substantial and credible if overseas deliveries hit 1.5M+ units in FY2026 and FCF margins normalise toward 7.5% post-capex-cycle.
The probability-weighted IV of HKD 89.86 (+23.7%) suggests BYD is modestly undervalued at current prices, with the asymmetry favouring bulls.

Sensitivity analysis shows BYD is priced for WACC ~11-12% and terminal growth ~2.0-3.0%, consistent with a moderately pessimistic outlook. Re-rating to WACC 10% (bull) would imply HKD 94.5-107.6 on base growth assumptions alone.

The 15% CAGR entry price on base assumptions is HKD 51.58 — 29% below current — indicating the current price does not offer a 15% return if only the base case materialises. The bull case entry price is HKD 103.22 (above current), meaning buyers today would achieve >15% CAGR in the bull scenario.

Q2 2026 results (expected August 2026) are the critical near-term catalyst — Citigroup estimates core net profit could recover to ~RMB 11.3bn, which would confirm the Q1 trough thesis and support valuation re-rating.

May 2026 data point: overseas hit a record 160,644 units (+80.4% YoY), now 42.6% of monthly sales mix — the first time overseas exceeded 40%. This is a significant positive data point that partially validates the bull case export thesis.
